prompt: Write snapshot(Object) using reflection -- getDeclaredFields plus setAccessible -- to map every declared field name to its current value, private fields included. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: getDeclaredFields() returns every field a class declares regardless of access level (unlike getFields(), which returns only public ones, including inherited), and setAccessible(true) is what suspends the private check so field.get(o) can read the value. Primitive fields come back boxed, so an int arrives as an Integer and a double as a Double, which is why the map is typed Map<String, Object>. Skipping synthetic fields keeps compiler-generated members out of the snapshot, and field.get throws the checked IllegalAccessException, so the loop has to handle it. This is the machinery behind debuggers, JSON serializers, and dependency-injection frameworks.
hints: Loop with `for (Field field : o.getClass().getDeclaredFields())` and `continue` on field.isSynthetic().
Call field.setAccessible(true) before field.get(o), otherwise reading a private field throws IllegalAccessException.
field.get(o) is declared to throw IllegalAccessException, so wrap it in a try/catch -- a LinkedHashMap keeps the fields in declaration order.
